correctness.rationale: Solving the predator fixed-point equation gives \(v=q(bu+c)\) with \(q=(\alpha-d)/a\). Substitution into the prey equation independently reproduces exactly the published quadratic coefficients. Since \(C_0>0\), Vieta's formulas and the discriminant give the complete positive-root classification, including the boundary \(C_2=0\) case. Fresh symbolic expansion verifies the multiplier identity. At the rational witness \((r,K,\beta,\gamma,a,b,c,k,\alpha,d)=(1,10,1/5,1,1,1/10,5,1/100,3/2,1/2)\), the quadratic has coefficients \((5001/5000,-439/50,1/2)\), discriminant \(9386/125\), and two positive roots approximately \(0.05732\) and \(8.72092\).

final_claim: For the Du–Han–Lei discrete fear-modulated predator-prey map with \(\alpha>d\), positive equilibria correspond exactly to positive roots of the published quadratic \(C_0u^2+C_1u+C_2\); the signs of \(C_2,C_1\) and the discriminant give the stated exhaustive zero/one/two-positive-root classification, and \(C_2=-K\gamma(1+kqc)\log\lambda_u\), allowing two coexistence equilibria even when prey cannot invade the predator-only equilibrium.
limitations: The theorem classifies existence and multiplicity of positive equilibria, not their full local or global stability.
It applies to the exact Du–Han–Lei map and parameter assumptions.
